turns.prompt: Compare an array (like a Python list) and a singly linked list for two tasks: reading the 1,000th element, and inserting a new element at the very front. Which structure is faster for each task, and why?
turns.answer: Reading the 1,000th element is constant‑time in an array because the index can be translated directly into a memory offset (O(1)), while a singly linked list requires traversing 999 next‑pointers from the head, which is linear time (O(n)). Inserting a new element at the front is O(1) for a linked list – you just create a node and point its next to the old head – but O(n) for an array because all existing elements must be shifted one position to make room.
